value.notes: The cases enumerate recognizers, including categories whose general executable construction is not established. Consult each type’s support boundary before using a configured value pattern.

text.notes: Recognizes a Text token. Ordinary source Text and typed scalar/native-byte emission are implemented; preserve literal bytes and distinguish framing escapes from general string escapes.

number.notes: Recognizes a binary64 Number token, not a %-delimited source literal. Range, finite-value and native encoding boundaries remain stage-specific.

truth.notes: Recognizes a Truth token loaded from lowercase true/false. This pattern does not introduce ?-delimited source literals or implicit truthiness.

null.notes: Explicit Null initializes an absence value and prints null. It is distinct from an unassigned slot and from internal None/Unknown states.

type.notes: Matches the native type token category. Construction and usable values depend on the explicit source type whitelist, descriptor binding and selected category.

list.notes: Typed owned Lists construct, append, replace and read indexed values; heterogeneous construction infers Thing without coercion. Indices and complete element types are checked. Iteration/removal remain outside this API.

dict.notes: Recognizes Dictionary type/storage structure. Namespace members and imports are demonstrated; arbitrary runtime map operations are not thereby supported.

definitive.notes: References preserve canonical declaration/member identity. A reference must resolve in its owning scope; the value category independently determines permitted use.

subject.notes: A subject participates in declaration/binding and paragraph antecedent selection. Its cases distinguish declared names, resolved references and definitions.

type.notes: A quoted declaration plus typed declarative phrase. Native whitelist and construction rules determine the represented category.

declarative.notes: A quoted name and definitive declarative phrase participate in typed registration/construction.

definitional.notes: A quoted name with a definitional Text phrase must satisfy paired framing and typed definition parsing.

value.notes: A quoted name and value phrase retain the concrete value category and assignment/definite-assignment boundaries.

declaration.notes: A quoted name may carry an optional phrase. Registration ownership and context determine whether that site is a usable declaration.

definitive.notes: A resolved identifier preserves its selected owner and canonical declaration; it is not a fresh declaration.

reference.notes: A #~# type token selects a native category rather than a quoted source identifier. Its supported role depends on the enclosing grammar.

definition.notes: A resolved definition and generic phrase preserve source ownership, bound parameters and permitted composition.

directive.notes: A quoted action label followed by a for/directive body records ordered source actions and typed any-parameters.

utilization.notes: A quoted label with a to/utilization phrase defines native text or a supported action relation; it is not an import provider phrase.

callable.notes: An encapsulated paragraph begins with the ordinary Function declaration and owns its body; public visibility exposes the Function, not its parameters.

signature.notes: A quoted parameter name is paired with a complete runtime type or an existing callable signature.

phrase.dependency.notes: Source-provider ownership governs relative imports and expanded declarations. Grammatical dependency attachment does not override those ownership rules.
